Subject: RFP Q: audit log retention, export formats, and chain-of-custody evidence

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We have a short set of clarifying questions focused on audit logs and exportability for our compliance team. Attached is our question set (Zenith_RFP_questions_v3.pdf). High-level asks:

- Confirm default and maximum retention window for audit logs (admin, system events, model invocation meta).
- Supported export formats (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet) and whether exports include full event payloads or are metadata-only.
- Can exports be produced with tamper-evident signature / chaining (hash chain) and what the delivery method is (S3, signed HTTPS).
- Is there a documented chain-of-custody procedure for preserving timestamps and origin IPs when exports are produced?
- Options for on-demand vs scheduled bulk exports, and any performance/size limits.

Could you provide concise answers plus any evidence artifacts (sample export file, playbook, or statement of process)? Our compliance deadline for the RFP is next Friday, 2027-04-16. If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call to walk through.

Best,
Alexandra Cruz

Olga — I filled out the technical sections and attached the export playbook and a sanitized sample export. Highlights:

- Retention: default 90 days for invocation logs, 365 days for admin/system events. Customers can configure retention per-tenant up to 7 years via Dedicated/Private contracts; hosted tenants can request extended retention via support agreement (we map to their account).
- Export formats: NDJSON (canonical, includes full event payload + metadata), CSV (selected metadata columns only), Parquet (optimized bulk with schema). Exports preserve field-level timestamps, tenant id, request id (trace id), and source IP where available.
- Tamper-evidence: we support a signed export manifest. Each export bundle includes an index.jsonl and an index.sha256 signature file signed with our export key; we also optionally provide a SHA256 chain (hash chain) per-bundle on request for high-assurance customers.
- Delivery: S3 (pre-signed, in customer region where possible), HTTPS downloadable link with expiring token, or direct SCP to customer endpoint for Private installs. Bulk job ETA: small (<10GB) within 4–6 hours; medium (10–200GB) 24–48 hours; large (>200GB) 48–72+ hours depending on queue and retention search cost.
- Chain-of-custody: export request is recorded as a first-class audit event (requestor identity, request timestamp, job id). Export job lifecycle (queued, running, delivered) emits events retained in our system; the delivered bundle also contains a manifest with timestamps and signing metadata.

Attached artifacts: audit_export_playbook.pdf (sanitized sample manifest and playbook steps), retention_matrix.csv (matrix by record class). I noted a couple of outstanding items where we may want confirmation from security: whether we can include origin IP consistently for GDPR-constrained tenants and whether we should redact certain payload fields by default.

- Rachel

Attachment: audit_export_playbook.pdf (PDF, 220 KB)
Attachment: retention_matrix.csv (CSV, 6 KB)

Hi Alexandra — thanks for the clear questions and for the deadline reminder. We reviewed internally and have attached a concise RFI response and supporting artifacts. Summary below and attachments included.

Summary (short answers)
- Retention: default windows: Invocation logs = 90 days; Admin & system events = 365 days. Max configurable retention up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private customers or via enterprise addendum for hosted accounts.
- Export formats: NDJSON (full payload + metadata), Parquet (optimized bulk), CSV (metadata-only exports).
- Tamper-evidence & manifest: every export includes an index.jsonl manifest and an index.sha256 signature file. For higher assurance customers we provide a signed bundle manifest and optional hash-chain artifact.
- Delivery: pre-signed S3 (preferred), expiring HTTPS link, or direct transfer for Private installations. Bulk export ETA guidance included in attachment.
- Chain-of-custody: export requests are recorded as first-class audit events with requestor identity and timestamp; job lifecycle events are retained; the delivered bundle contains a signed manifest with timestamps and signer id.

Deliverables attached to this message:
- Draft_RFI_response_v1.docx (our short-form RFI response tailored to Zenith)
- audit_export_playbook.pdf (sanitized playbook with sample manifest and a sample export bundle manifest)
- retention_matrix.csv (retention table by record class)

Next steps: If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk through manifests and the chain-of-custody flow. Otherwise I'm happy to provide additional sanitized sample exports and a signed statement for the RFP packet.
